Their cathodes are driven through current-limit resistors by CM4 status outputs: D19 via R93 from PI_nLED_Activity, D22 via R89 from Ethernet_nLED2, D43 via R34 from Ethernet_nLED3.",
      "expected": "The CM4 nLED outputs are active-low, so each LED anode must be tied to a supply (+3V3). Other status LEDs in the design (e.g. D24, D26, D48) have their anodes tied to +3V3 directly or through a resistor. These three LEDs should have the same connection.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"30\") (name \"/NET0106\") (class \"Default\") (node (ref \"D19\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D22\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")) (node (ref \"D43\") (pin \"2\") (pinfunction \"A\") (pintype \"passive\")))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (code \"101\") (name \"NET0123\") ... (node (ref \"Module2\") (pin \"21\") (pinfunction \"PI_nLED_Activity\") (pintype \"open_collector\")) (node (ref \"R93\") (pin \"1\") ...)"}
      ],
      "impact": "With no anode supply, D19, D22 and D43 cannot light. The PI activity and Ethernet link/activity indicators will be dead.",
      "confidence": 0.5
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R100"],
      "pins": ["R100.1", "R100.2"],
      "nets": ["VOUTN", "VOUTP"],
      "observed": "R100 is valued 24k, but its library description and MPN describe a 24 Ω part: the MPN is FRC0805J240TSD and the description reads '5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor'.",
      "expected": "The value field should match the purchased part, 24 Ω. A 24 kΩ bleeder across VOUTN/VOUTP would differ by three orders of magnitude from the intended part.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(comp (ref \"R100\") (value \"24k\") (footprint \"Resistor_SMD:R_0805_2012Metric\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(description \" 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS\")"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(property (name \"MPN\") (value \"FRC0805J240TSD\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "If the 24k value is the mistake, the load/bleed current on the VOUTP/VOUTN rail is far lower than intended. If the part is the mistake, it is a much heavier load than intended.",
      "confidence": 0.4
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["U34", "U36"],
      "pins": ["U34.4", "U34.5", "U36.4", "U36.5"],
      "nets": ["GND"],
      "observed": "On both isolated CAN transceivers U34 and U36, GND1 (pin 4) and GND2 (pin 5) are both on the single GND net. No isolated ground net exists in the netlist.",
      "expected": "The spec describes isolated CAN buses. An isolated transceiver needs its bus-side ground (GND2) to be separate from the logic-side ground (GND1). Joining them defeats the isolation barrier.",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U34\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"GND1\") (pintype \"power_in\")) (node (ref \"U34\") (pin \"5\") (pinfunction \"GND2\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(node (ref \"U36\") (pin \"4\") (pinfunction \"GND1\") (pintype \"power_in\")) (node (ref \"U36\") (pin \"5\") (pinfunction \"GND2\") (pintype \"power_in\"))"},
        {"source": "spec", "quote": "two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver"}
      ],
      "impact": "The CAN bus ground is no longer isolated from the logic ground. Ground loops and common-mode faults from the motor side can reach the CM4 and its logic, which defeats the stated isolation.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    }
  ],
  "summary": "The most likely anomaly is that the anodes of three status LEDs (D19, D22, D43) sit on a net with no other connection, so they have no supply. Lower-confidence candidates are R100 valued 24k against a 24 Ω part, and the isolated CAN transceivers having GND1 and GND2 tied to the same ground."
}

anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three status LEDs D19 (green), D22 (yellow) and D43 (green) are all on /NET0106, and that net has no other connections. Their cathodes are driven through current-limit resistors by CM4 status outputs: D19 via R93 from PI_nLED_Activity, D22 via R89 from Ethernet_nLED2, D43 via R34 from Ethernet_nLED3.
anomalies.expected: The CM4 nLED outputs are active-low, so each LED anode must be tied to a supply (+3V3). Other status LEDs in the design (e.g. D24, D26, D48) have their anodes tied to +3V3 directly or through a resistor. These three LEDs should have the same connection.
anomalies.impact: With no anode supply, D19, D22 and D43 cannot light. The PI activity and Ethernet link/activity indicators will be dead.

anomalies.observed: R100 is valued 24k, but its library description and MPN describe a 24 Ω part: the MPN is FRC0805J240TSD and the description reads '5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor'.
anomalies.expected: The value field should match the purchased part, 24 Ω. A 24 kΩ bleeder across VOUTN/VOUTP would differ by three orders of magnitude from the intended part.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24k value is the mistake, the load/bleed current on the VOUTP/VOUTN rail is far lower than intended. If the part is the mistake, it is a much heavier load than intended.

anomalies.observed: On both isolated CAN transceivers U34 and U36, GND1 (pin 4) and GND2 (pin 5) are both on the single GND net. No isolated ground net exists in the netlist.
anomalies.expected: The spec describes isolated CAN buses. An isolated transceiver needs its bus-side ground (GND2) to be separate from the logic-side ground (GND1). Joining them defeats the isolation barrier.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller ... through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The CAN bus ground is no longer isolated from the logic ground. Ground loops and common-mode faults from the motor side can reach the CM4 and its logic, which defeats the stated isolation.

parsed.summary: The most likely anomaly is that the anodes of three status LEDs (D19, D22, D43) sit on a net with no other connection, so they have no supply. Lower-confidence candidates are R100 valued 24k against a 24 Ω part, and the isolated CAN transceivers having GND1 and GND2 tied to the same ground.
